source_derived_summary: Zhang et al. (2013, pp.251–253) describe 2 g Ti (≥99.5 wt%, stated average 0.25 mm), 40 mL 28 wt% aqueous ammonia and 80 mL 30 wt% peroxide stirred at 0–5 °C for 3 h; 100 mL 2 wt% F68 solution follows (2 h stirring, 12 h rest), then 70 °C/0.5 h, 100 mL ethanol, centrifugation and 200 °C/2 h calcination. Reduction is hydrogen-atmosphere reported, but the post-calcination precursor remains named H4TiO5. XRD supports author-reported Ti4O7 at 850 °C/5 h or 860 °C/4 h (Fig.1). At 850 °C, SEM diameters are 200–500 nm and BET area 8.351 m²/g (Fig.2). The text’s XRD crystallite estimates disagree: 100–150 nm versus about160 nm. Room-temperature diffuse-reflectance spectra span 200–1100 nm, with UV and visible/near-infrared bands (Fig.3); oxygen-vacancy causation is interpretation. Conductivity is background, not measured here. Unspecified details include hydrogen flow/purity/pressure, ramps, cooling/passivation, BET conditioning and exhaustive retained inventory. Phase purity does not establish elemental exclusivity. The reader footer attributes IET 2013; permissive reuse is unestablished.
